scope: Compact restoration of Newton polytopes, support functions and the CPWL DC pair, plus reference-based shortening in Chapters 03, 05 and 07. Read-only source review; only review metadata and receipts updated.
findings: The Newton definition fixes a nonempty finite max-affine family. The ordinary hull records slopes only; the lifted hull records slopes and intercepts. No canonical uniqueness of the lifted hull is claimed.
The support maximum is well-defined for nonempty compact convex sets. The finite-hull generator argument proves p(x)=h_Nhat(p)(x,1); the unlifted equation is explicitly limited to zero intercepts.

Adding two maxima expands into all pairwise sums; taking their maximum collects all terms. Convex hulls therefore obey the stated Minkowski/hull identities. The concise proof retains the required reasoning.

Every scalar convex CPWL function admits a finite max-affine representation by its full-dimensional affine pieces, which are global supporting affine functions. Applying the two lifted support identities proves the general f=g-h equation, including biased functions.

The Chapter 03 application explicitly uses doubled inputs and convex CPWL ReLU streams, retaining biases through lifting. It does not extend the polytope representation to non-CPWL smooth activations.

Exactly six previously retired labels are restored. Their actual pinned declarations support the definitions and calculus equations; the general biased two-polytope consequence has a new unbadged label. The narrower bias-free network theorem remains retired.

The one shortened Chapter 03 proof invokes the same general network theorem and ReLU identity, retaining the identity-output convention and l=L endpoint. The omitted composition reminder is already stated and proved in foundations.
The Chapter 05 ICNN recap and Chapter 07 Maxout recap now refer to their retained foundation definitions. Their mathematical content and citation keys remain available there.
All 143 existing display blocks across the four chapters are retained byte-for-byte in their original order. All existing labels, aliases and Lean badges are retained; no old proof is deleted.

follow_ups.scope: Brief max-plus introduction and one unnumbered polynomial display; duplicate max-affine definition removed.
findings: The max-plus operations are maximum and ordinary addition on the extended domain. Real powers are explicitly restricted to finite inputs and mean scalar multiplication; no operation involving negative real powers at minus infinity is asserted.

A monomial evaluates to b_r plus the scalar product a_r^T x. Finite tropical addition therefore gives exactly the displayed finite max-affine function. The finite nonempty condition N>=1, real coefficients, and fixed representation needed by the Newton definition are retained.
The added display is unbadged and does not reactivate any further retired label or claim a new Lean proof. All support, lifted-polytope and DC formulas retain their reviewed scope.
